Description: With some guidance students will be able to elicit requirements and model solutions to deliver value with respect to a problem domain. Identify and explore opportunities for enterprise and innovation in a commercial and economic context.
With some guidance students will be able to use appropriate ethical and legal frameworks, recognise and assess potential ethical and social issues associated with technology.
With some guidance students will be able to use specified development tools and follow defined processes to develop, debug and formally test software individually and as part of a team.

With some guidance students will be able to use a variety of software development methodologies to model networked and stand-alone information and database systems. Demonstrate appropriate consideration of user experience and Human Computer Interaction approaches. Develop systems using appropriate software design patterns.

With some guidance students will be able to participate constructively in team organisation and operation, with some awareness of contemporary theories of teamworking dynamics. Be responsible for delivery of defined elements of group projects. Reflect critically on team and individual performance.

With some guidance students will be able to review, reflect and document consequences of personal decisions that impact upon their capacity to study effectively and on their general well-being. Review, reflect, plan and document a professional portfolio of experience.
